subject: Meteorology
title: Multicell Clusters
description: A quick, practical guide to Multicell Clusters.

hook.text: Multicell clusters are groups of storms where new cells keep forming as old ones die—a self-renewing system.

buildup.text: Each cell goes through the same life cycle, but the group persists because outflow triggers fresh updrafts.

discovery.text: New cells typically form on the upwind or warm side of the cluster—following the moisture and instability.

twist.text: The cluster can look like one big blob on radar, but it's actually several storms at different life stages.

climax.text: Multicell clusters can produce moderate hail, heavy rain, and occasional severe wind gusts.

punchline.text: One storm dies, another is born—the cluster lives on.

quiz.question: How do multicell clusters sustain themselves?
options: Outflow from dying cells triggers new cells
They absorb energy from the jet stream
